THE WORKFLOW

From the shift record
to the agreed charges.

A daily report explains more than the metres drilled. Keep the hours, crew, consumables and delays available when the work is reviewed.

01 /

Record the shift.

Capture the rig, hole, depths, activity timeline, crew and consumables. Save a draft or submit the report when it is ready.

02 /

Review with context.

Approve a report, raise a query or reject it with a reason. Keep the review history with the work it describes.

03 /

Understand the charges.

Inspect the recorded quantities and time against contract rates. Follow the detail from the report into the charge breakdown.

EOS / IN PRACTICE

A shift is more than a metre total.

Record the work as it happened.

The daily record

Capture the rig and hole, start and end depths, crew, time on activities, consumables and the interruptions that affected the shift. Keep those records together so a reviewer can understand how the reported result was achieved.

Draft, submit and review

Crews can prepare a draft before submitting the report. Reviewers can approve it, raise a query or reject it with a reason. The review belongs with the report, giving the next person the context needed to follow up.

Find the report you need

Use the report register and calendar to locate the relevant rig and day. Move from a period overview back into the daily records when a number or an interruption needs explaining.

Production with the context intact.

Review the period, then follow the evidence.

Metres and operating time

Review recorded production and time usage for a selected period. Separate the drilling result from the hours and activity categories behind it, then inspect individual reports where more explanation is needed.

Completed holes and progress

Review the completed-hole records alongside the production report. Use the recorded evidence to understand what was completed during the period and how that relates to the selected program.

Recorded work and agreed charges

Inspect quantities and time against the contract rate records. Follow a charge back to the activity, crew or consumable record that supports it. The operational charge view remains distinct from the actual supplier invoices held in Account.

IN THE WORKSPACE

Work with the detail.

Plods and period reports

Find daily shift records and prepare reports for a selected period, project and contractor.

Approvals and queries

Keep review notes alongside the report so the crew can see what needs attention.

Production and time

Review recorded metres, operating hours and time usage for your selected program.

Rates and contracts

Maintain the rate library and contracts used to understand charges for the work completed.

PART OF DRILLOPS

Focused apps.
A shared working context.

Invoice records and purchase orders belong in Account. Program planning and training belong in Project.

EOS, Account and Project use the same organisation login and underlying project data.

QUESTIONS

Before you get started.

Who is EOS for?

Crews preparing drilling reports, clients reviewing submitted work, and operations teams examining production, time and charges.

Does EOS replace the invoice ledger?

No. EOS explains recorded work and its associated charges. Account holds invoice and credit records, purchasing information and financial review tools.

How does access work?

Sign in with the account supplied by your organisation. The clients, projects and operational records available to you depend on that account’s permissions.
